title: ConnectWise Suspends Cloud Services in Response to Cyberattack
description: ConnectWise suspended its Cloud Backup, SaaS Security, and Cloud Management services following a cyberattack involving compromised credentials that allowed unauthorized access to Microsoft 365 tenants. The attacker used a stolen Cloud Backup credential to sign into numerous tenants, with evidence of scripted access attempts and privilege escalations. ConnectWise shut down affected services to contain the incident and continues remediation and security validation. Customers' backups remain encrypted and protected, with no evidence of unauthorized access to backup data. The company has not provided a timeline for service restoration.
aiSummary: ConnectWise experienced a cyberattack where a compromised Cloud Backup credential was used to access Microsoft 365 tenants between October 15 and 16, 2026. The attacker leveraged a client assertion credential residing in ConnectWise's tenant to authenticate into at least 162 Microsoft 365 tenants, originating from an IP address previously used in password spraying attacks. The attacker performed scripted sign-ins in sorted GUID order, indicating automated targeting. Privilege escalation was observed in at least one tenant, where the ConnectWise Cloud Management app added itself to the Global Administrator role and created new client secrets. ConnectWise responded by suspending Cloud Backup, SaaS Security, and Cloud Management services to mitigate the attack. The company confirmed backups remain encrypted and protected, with no evidence of unauthorized access to backup data. The incident is ongoing with remediation and security validation in progress.
aiImpact: The attack resulted in unauthorized access to Microsoft 365 tenants via compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup credentials, potentially exposing tenant configurations and administrative privileges. Although backups remain encrypted and protected with no evidence of compromise, the incident disrupted Cloud Backup, SaaS Security, and Cloud Management services, impacting scheduled backups, archive access, restores, monitoring, alerting, and user/license management. The attacker gained elevated privileges in some tenants, which could allow configuration changes or persistence mechanisms. The full extent of tenant-level impact depends on individual tenant configurations and whether the ConnectWise service principals were present.
